discussion_comments.comment_body: There issue for `bearer_token` here is that it will give you a token that is only valid for a second.  `modelRuntime.getAuth` ideally should ensure that the token it gives out is valid for at least 30 minutes (I think it should be able to guarantee that).  Not sure if we should do this in general or just this case.  Probably makes sense to proactive refresh?  Maybe something to discuss with the clanker.

> There issue for `bearer_token` here is that it will give you a token that is only valid for a second. `modelRuntime.getAuth` ideally should ensure that the token it gives out is valid for at least 30 minutes (I think it should be able to guarantee that). Not sure if we should do this in general or just this case. Probably makes sense to proactive refresh? Maybe something to discuss with the clanker.

Some providers refresh before expiry on their side, e.g. Codex:

- Constant: [CHATGPT_ACCESS_TOKEN_REFRESH_WINDOW_MINUTES: i64 = 5](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/login/src/auth/manager.rs#L182-L183)
- Refresh check: parses the access-token JWT expiry and refreshes when [expires_at <= now + 5   minutes](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/login/src/auth/manager.rs#L2521-L2527).

And others, like Anthropic, are not documented -  Pi’s Anthropic OAuth exchange/refresh fixtures use `expires_in: 3600`, then Pi applies a 5-minute skew, so Pi treats a newly issued token as usable for ~55 minutes. So I'd keep `getAuth` to refresh if within 5 minutes instead of 30 bc half of Anthropic's time window, so too often, then keep 30 for Radius (default CLI commands to 30 mins, but also add minimum time to expiry as a command flag).

Each temp dir is unique, so the files for the editor would be this:

```
/tmp/pi-editor-A1b2C3/prompt.md
/tmp/pi-editor-X9y8Z7/prompt.md
```

Previously it was `/tmp/pi-extension-editor-${Date.now()}.md`, so this should in theory provide more safety against collisions afaik.

Question is, if the folder per external editor session is overkill and a per pi instance would be preferable.
We should generally not use `tmpdir()` because of all the security nonsense that comes with it.  I think we already have a `.pi/agent/tmp` folder now?  Maybe i misremember.

Addressed in `3e6aa2f6`. `getAgentDir()` is the canonical helper and respects `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`. The existing `<agentDir>/tmp/extensions` path is specific to temporary extension installations, so external-editor prompts now use a separate `<agentDir>/tmp/external-editor` root. That root is forced to mode `0700`, while each invocation still gets its own private `mkdtempSync()` directory.
There're more occurrences of `tmpdir()` in other parts of the codebase. Worth a follow-up.
Fixed in 2605fa6c — control characters (`\x00-\x1f`, `\x7f`) are now stripped from `token.href` before embedding in the OSC 8 sequence.
